questions.question:
Choose the one word substitute for the below sentence.

Mia asked her cousin, a person who is in charge of a museum called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Curator**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Curator"** refers to a person who is in charge of a museum, art collection, or archive. They are responsible for acquiring, caring for, and displaying collections. (संग्रहालय के प्रभारी) 
 
 
• **Example:** The curator organized a special exhibition on ancient Egyptian artifacts.
 
 
 
• In the given question, Mia asked her cousin about the person in charge of a museum, which directly corresponds to the role of a curator. (संग्रहालय के प्रभारी का कार्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Curator**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Conservator** (रक्षक): A person responsible for the preservation and repair of works of art, books, or other artifacts.
 
 
• **Example:** The conservator restored the painting to its original condition.
 
 
 
• **Director** (निर्देशक): A person who manages and oversees the operations of an institution, company, or project.
 
 
• **Example:** The director approved the budget for the museum's expansion project.
 
 
 
• **Historian** (इतिहासकार): A person who studies and writes about history.
 
 
• **Example:** The historian gave a lecture on the impact of World War II on Europe.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect sentence.

options.text: Ten percent of the students in the class speak three languages.
Forty-five minutes is a very long coffee break.
His advice was perfect for the situation.
The academic committee were undivided in their decision to hire the new staff.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**To identify the incorrect sentence, let's analyze the subject-verb agreement and noun usage in each option:**

__
 
• **Option 1: Ten percent of the students in the class speak three languages.**

 
 
• When a percentage is followed by a plural noun (students), it takes a plural verb (speak).
 
• This sentence is grammatically correct__.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Forty-five minutes is a very long coffee break.**
 __
 
• Units of time, money, and distance are treated as a single collective unit and take a singular verb.
 
• This sentence is grammatically correct__.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: His advice was perfect for the situation.**
 __
 
• "Advice" is an uncountable (mass) noun and must always be paired with a singular verb.
 
• This sentence is grammatically correct__.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: The academic committee were undivided in their decision to hire the new staff.**
 __
 
• The sentence is erroneous__. A collective noun like "committee" takes a singular verb when the group acts as a single, unified entity. The use of the word "undivided" explicitly indicates that the group is acting as one unit.
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "The academic committee **was** undivided in **its** decision to hire the new staff."
 
 
 
• __Therefore, out of the given options, only sentence 4 is grammatically incorrect__.

questions.question:

Please submit your assignments __by Friday__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**No substitution**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The preposition "**by**" is used to indicate a deadline or the latest time by which something must be done.
 
• In the context of submitting assignments, "**by Friday**" correctly implies that the work must be submitted at any time before or on Friday.
 
• **Options 1, 2**, and **3** do not follow standard English usage for setting a deadline in this specific sentence structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"Please submit your assignments **by**__ Friday."*

• **Option 1 & 2: "till" and "until"** are used to describe a continuous state or action that lasts up to a certain point (e.g., "I will stay until Friday"). They are not used for one-time completion deadlines.
 
• **Option 3: "at Friday"** is grammatically incorrect; the preposition "at" is used for specific times (e.g., at 3 PM), while "on" is used for days of the week.

questions.question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the Sentence:**

The old woman watered the plants every morning.

options.text: The plants was watered by the old woman every morning.
The plants were watered by the old woman every morning.
The plants are watered by the old woman every morning.
The plants had been watered by the old woman every morning.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tense Identification:** The original sentence "watered" is in the **Simple Past** tense.
 
• **Passive Voice Rule:** To convert Simple Past to Passive, the structure used is "**was/were + past participle (V3)**".
 
• **Subject-Object Swap:** The object of the active sentence ("the plants") becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:** Since the new subject "the plants" is plural, we must use the auxiliary verb "**were**" instead of "was."
 
• **Consistency:** The frequency phrase "every morning" remains in its position to maintain the original meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The plants were watered by the old woman every morning."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "The plants was watered..." is grammatically incorrect because "was" cannot be used with the plural subject "plants."
 
• **Option 3:** "The plants are watered..." is in the Simple Present Passive, which changes the tense from the past to the present.
 
• **Option 4:** "The plants had been watered..." is in the Past Perfect Passive, which implies the action was completed before another past event.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word:

**Foment**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Foment** means to **encourage, provoke, or stir up** trouble, conflict, or strong feelings.
 
• **Instigate** means to **incite or provoke someone to take a particular action**, especially an undesirable one.
 
• Since both words convey the idea of provoking or encouraging an action, **"instigate"** is the most appropriate synonym of **"foment"**.
 
• Hence, **Option 4** is the correct answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Instigate**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: Flare** – Means to burn brightly or suddenly become intense; it is not a synonym of *foment*.
 
• **Option 2: Bother** – Means to annoy or trouble someone.
 
• **Option 3: Quash** – Means to suppress, reject, or put an end to something; it is actually an antonym of *foment*.
 
• **Option 4: Instigate** – Means to provoke, incite, or stir up an action, making it the closest synonym of *foment*.

questions.question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

The lady said to her friend, "When was the bridge built here on this river?"

options.text: The lady asked her friend when the bridge had been built there on this river.
The lady asked her friend when the bridge had been built there on that river.
The lady asked her friend when the bridge was built there on that river.
The lady asked her friend when the bridge have been built there on that river.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** The lady said to her friend, "When was the bridge built here on this river?"
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• The phrase **"said to"** changes to **"asked"** because the sentence is an interrogative (a question).
 
 
 
• **Tense Change (Simple Past to Past Perfect):**
 
 
• The simple past passive **"was built"** must be changed to the past perfect passive **"had been built"** because the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
 
 
• **Words Expressing Nearness:**
 
 
• **"here"** changes to **"there"**.
 
• **"this"** changes to **"that"**.
 
 
 
• **Sentence Structure:**
 
 
• The question format (was the bridge built) changes to an assertive format (the bridge had been built). The question mark is replaced by a full stop.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The lady asked her friend when the bridge had been built there on that river."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect because it fails to change "this" to "that."
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect because it retains the simple past tense "was built" instead of back-shifting to the past perfect.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect because "have been built" is grammatically wrong in this context and is not a past perfect form.

questions.question:
**Change the following sentence into the Active form.**

It has been being debated for months whether the new enacted or not.

options.text: They have been debating for months whether the new law will be enacted or not.
The new law will be enacted or not, which they have been debating for months.
Whether the new law will be enacted or not has been debated for months.
They have been being debated for months whether the new law will be enacted or not.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tense Identification:** The original sentence "has been being debated" is in the **Present Perfect Continuous Passive** voice.
 
• **Active Voice Rule:** To convert Present Perfect Continuous Passive to Active, the structure changes from "has/have been being + V3" to "**has/have been + V1-ing**".
 
• **Subject Placement:** Since the passive sentence uses the dummy subject "It," we introduce a logical subject like "They" to perform the action in the active voice.
 
• **Completing the Context:** While the original prompt had a slight typo ("whether the new enacted or not"), Option 1 correctly restores the likely intended meaning by adding "law will be."
 
• **Verb Conversion:** "Has been being debated" becomes "have been debating" to match the plural subject "They."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"They have been debating for months whether the new law will be enacted or not."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** This is a complex sentence that rearranges the clauses but does not properly address the active transformation of the main verb.
 
• **Option 3:** This sentence is still in the **Passive Voice** ("has been debated"), just using the "whether" clause as the subject.
 
• **Option 4:** "Have been being debated" is still passive and grammatically redundant in this active context.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.**

He said, "What are you doing today?"

options.text: He asked what I was doing that day.
He asked what was I doing that day.
He asked me what I was doing today.
He asked what I was doing today.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** He said, "What are you doing today?"
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• Since the sentence is a question, the reporting verb **"said"** is changed to **"asked"**.
 
 
 
• **Conjunction:**
 
 
• In "Wh-" questions, no external conjunction (like 'that' or 'if') is used. The question word **"what"** acts as the connector.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:**
 
 
• The second-person pronoun **"you"** is changed based on the object of the reporting verb. Since no object is mentioned, it is common to assume the speaker is talking to "me," so "you" becomes **"I"**.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change (Present Continuous to Past Continuous):**
 
 
• The present continuous **"are doing"** changes to the past continuous **"was doing"** because the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
 
 
• **Time Expression:**
 
 
• The word **"today"** is changed to **"that day"** in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Sentence Structure:**
 
 
• The interrogative form (Verb + Subject) is changed to an assertive form (Subject + Verb). Therefore, "are you doing" becomes "I was doing."
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He asked what I was doing that day."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "He asked what was I doing that day." 

 
 
• Incorrect because it maintains the interrogative word order (Verb + Subject) instead of the assertive word order (Subject + Verb).
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He asked me what I was doing today." 
 
 
• Incorrect because it fails to change the time expression "today" to "that day."
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He asked what I was doing today." 
 
 
• Incorrect because it also fails to change "today" to "that day."

questions.question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

We have visited Paris many times.

options.text: Paris was visited by us many times.
Paris has been visited by us many times.
Paris had been visited by us many times.
Paris is visited by us many times.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tense Identification:** The original sentence "have visited" is in the **Present Perfect** tense.
 
• **Passive Voice Rule:** For the Present Perfect tense, the passive structure is "**has/have + been + past participle (V3)**".
 
• **Subject-Object Swap:** The object "Paris" moves to the subject position, and the subject "We" becomes the agent "by us."
 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:** While the original subject "We" used "have," the new subject "Paris" is singular and requires the auxiliary verb "**has**."
 
• **Maintaining Adverbs:** The phrase "many times" is kept at the end to preserve the original meaning of frequency.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Paris has been visited by us many times."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "was visited" is the Simple Past Passive, which loses the "present relevance" of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 3:** "had been visited" is the Past Perfect Passive, which is used for actions completed before another point in the past.
 
• **Option 4:** "is visited" is the Simple Present Passive, which implies a general fact or habit rather than a completed experience.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

She said that she would not leave her job.

options.text: She said, "I will not leave my job."
She said, "She would not leave her job."
She said, "I would not leave my job."
She said, "She will not leave her job."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She said that she would not leave her job.
 
• **Key Conversions from Indirect to Direct:**
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:**
 
 
• The third-person pronoun **"she"** in the reported speech refers back to the subject of the reporting verb ("She"). Therefore, in direct speech, it reverts to the first-person pronoun **"I"**.
 
• Similarly, the possessive adjective **"her"** reverts to **"my"**.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change (Would to Will):**
 
 
• When moving from indirect to direct speech, the conditional/past modal **"would"** is changed back to the future modal **"will"** to reflect the speaker's original words.
 
 
 
• **Removal of Conjunction:**
 
 
• The conjunction **"that"** is removed and replaced by a comma and quotation marks.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She said, 'I will not leave my job.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect because it keeps the sentence in the third person ("She") and retains "would," which is essentially just the indirect speech placed in quotes.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect because it uses "would" instead of "will." In direct speech, a person expressing a future intention would use "will."
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect because it uses the third-person pronoun "She," making it sound like she is talking about someone else's job.

questions.question: Which of the following conjunctions is NOT used in the passage?

questions.question: Identify the sentence from the passage that contains a relative pronoun, and choose the correct type of pronoun used.

options.text: Plastic surgery has become increasingly common in recent years.
While advancements in medical technology have made surgeries safer and more accessible...
Many people develop an unrealistic expectation, which often leads to dissatisfaction...
An excessive focus on outward beauty can promote superficial values in society.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 3: "Many people develop an unrealistic expectation, which__ often leads to dissatisfaction..."***

 __
 
• The word **"which"** is used in this sentence.
 
• **"Which"** is a **relative pronoun** because it introduces a relative clause and refers back to the noun phrase *"unrealistic expectation"*.
 
• The clause *"which often leads to dissatisfaction"* gives additional information about the expectation.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: "Plastic surgery has become increasingly common in recent years."***
 
 
• This sentence does **not contain any pronoun**, particularly no relative pronoun.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: "While advancements in medical technology have made surgeries safer and more accessible..."***
 
 
• The word **"While"** is a **subordinating conjunction**, not a pronoun.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: "An excessive focus on outward beauty can promote superficial values in society."***
 
 
• This sentence also does **not contain a relative pronoun**.
 
 

Therefore, the sentence containing a **relative pronoun** is in **Option 3**, where **"which"** functions as a relative pronoun.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Relative Pronoun:** A pronoun that introduces a relative clause and relates it to a noun mentioned earlier.
 
• **Common relative pronouns:** who, whom, whose, which, and that.
 
• Example: *"The book **which** I bought yesterday is very interesting."*
